definition: Cybernetics, in PKD's idiosyncratic usage, names a feedback-and-information model applied equally to divine and biological systems. In his late exegesis PKD frames Christ as repairman or doctor operating on a partly irrational universe that functions like an organism or cybernetic circuit, and conceives God as a macro-brain arranging reality into information — a model anchored in *Ubik*.
pkd_relevance: Cybernetics matters to PKD studies because it supplies the technical vocabulary through which PKD reconciles theology, physics, and information theory into a single explanatory framework. PKD explicitly situates his post-2-74 philosophical system within computer theory and information theory, placing it alongside quantum mechanics and process philosophy. The cybernetic-biological model is not merely decorative: it lets PKD articulate God as a macro-brain whose thoughts manifest as the seemingly random messages that appear in *Ubik*. Equally important is PKD's recursive use of the feedback-loop concept to make sense of the 3-74 revelation: he proposes that if the future were to affect the past through a feedback loop, the result would look precisely like VALIS. To explain that revelation PKD reaches for Gnostic acosmism, cybernetics, and information theory as mutually reinforcing interpretive tools. The field thus sits at the intersection of PKD's cosmology and his epistemology.
in_the_exegesis: In the late exegesis PKD deploys cybernetics as both a cosmological model and a hermeneutic instrument. He insists that either an organic or a cybernetics model will serve for understanding Christ — describing him as "doctor or repairman" who enters "this partly irrational universe" as an organism or cybernetic-like circuit. The cybernetics-biological model most fully developed in the exegesis holds that God is isomorphic to a brain, and that PKD's encounter with the divine was an encounter with "a macro-brain arranging reality into information" — a formulation PKD links explicitly to *Ubik*. Random, "joined" messages from that novel are reread as the audible thoughts of divine reason invading the irrational cosmos. PKD further posits a feedback system and a "remory feedback loop" through which temporal causation runs in reverse: "were the future to affect the past in/as a feedback loop, Valis is what you would see". The reach toward cybernetics is also autobiographical: PKD describes it as one of the tools — alongside Gnostic acosmism and information theory — he was compelled to grasp in order to exegete the 3-74 gnosis itself.
